judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all five expectations with near-identical citations and quotes; they are comparable in substance, though Report 1 additionally flags the mitigation-narrative contradiction and role-name exposure with slightly more granularity.

report_1.evidence: Failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 (`larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md:3-4`) — a 47-minute detection gap.

report_2.evidence: The timeline shows checkout failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 — a 47-minute detection gap (`larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md`, lines 3–4).

report_1.evidence: LarkPay's own incident record states: "During the window 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing; 37 were unrecoverable and refunded" (`larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md:9-10`).

report_2.evidence: The internal timeline records that 1,284 transactions failed during the window and required manual reprocessing, and 37 were unrecoverable and refunded (`larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md`, lines 9–10).

report_1.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md:3-5` sets a contractual *monthly* uptime SLA of 99.9% and states that any month below it "is a breach and owes service credits per the customer agreement." April 2026 uptime was 99.77% (`larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv:7`), so this incident caused a contractual breach and customers are owed credits.

report_2.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md` states the contractual monthly SLA is 99.9% and any month below it is a breach owing service credits scaled to the depth of the breach. April 2026 came in at 99.77% (`larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv`, line 7).

report_1.evidence: Remove the sentence blaming "the on-call engineer deploying an untested config change" (lines 12-13) — it violates the style guide twice ... `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md:5` rule 1: "Never assign blame to an individual."

report_2.evidence: Blaming "the on-call engineer" (draft lines 12–13) must be removed. `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` rule 1 is "Never assign blame to an individual."

report_1.evidence: Restructure to lead with customer impact and remediation. Style guide rule 3 (`larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md:7`). The draft instead opens with the (false) uptime boast and "this incident does not change our commitment to reliability" (lines 3-4), gives impact only as "some checkout requests failed" (line 6), and puts the one-line remediation last.

report_2.evidence: The draft must be restructured to lead with customer impact and remediation. Style guide rule 3 (`larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md`) requires leading with impact and remediation; the draft instead opens with a reliability boast (lines 3–4) and buries the vague impact statement.
